statements: The exhaust-color guidance in the HMMWV maintenance manual does not directly specify a diagnostic system for rough-running engines emitting white smoke.
According to standard vehicle maintenance knowledge, white exhaust smoke typically indicates coolant leakage into the combustion chamber.
A cracked cylinder head may cause coolant leakage into the combustion chamber.
A failed head gasket may cause coolant leakage into the combustion chamber.
The exhaust-color guidance referenced in TM 9-2320-280-20-1 generally directs the maintainer to the exhaust-color diagnostic system for rough running.
According to the exhaust-color diagnostic system, fuel system issues can cause rough running.
Clogged fuel filters are an example of a fuel system issue that can cause rough running.
Fuel pump failure is an example of a fuel system issue that can cause rough running.
According to the exhaust-color diagnostic system, ignition system problems can cause rough running.
Faulty spark plugs are an example of an ignition system problem that can cause rough running.
Faulty ignition coils are an example of an ignition system problem that can cause rough running.
